why: The big woodtype 'RED DEAD REDEMPTION 2' title lands hard, and the 'EGG 1 OF 12 · THE KRAKEN' toast makes me want to keep hunting. The photo itself is almost blank sepia noise, though: it looks like an image that failed to load, not one developing. The egg counter does the hooking here, not the section art.

A spyglass circle peeking at a lantern-lit ghost ship under a bold blackletter 'PIRATES OF THE CARIBBEAN' makes me want to see the rest of the ship. On the other hand, almost the whole frame is flat black, so the tease depends on that one circle.

The title says '3 IDIOTS · The Workshop', but the image is a stormy sea captioned 'The Kraken's Storm · Pirates of the Caribbean'. With no visible transition it reads as a mislabelled slide, and the image is mostly dark. I'm confused, not pulled in.

Same mismatch as H003, but the pale torn edge eating into the storm shows the old world being wiped away for the new one. That moment of change makes me want to see what is underneath. 'HERE BE MONSTERS' is a nice tease too.
A gold-rimmed spyglass reveals the Black Pearl's lit stern against a faintly visible dark sea, under 'IN FOUR ACTS / PIRATES OF THE CARIBBEAN'. It's a cinematic opening that promises a story.

The campfire image is beautiful, but the act title says 'HARRY POTTER' while the caption says 'The Campfire · Red Dead Redemption 2'. Nothing hints that a transition is coming, so it looks like a labelling error.
The bold RDR2 title is good, but the framed photo is a murky, grainy sepia smear with almost nothing legible. As a still it reads as a broken or loading image, not a scene.
A glowing burn-hole is eating through the RDR2 campfire photo under the 'HARRY POTTER' title. You can see the page burning from one world into the next, and I'd scroll to watch it finish.
